stem: Which is a typical characteristic of an unplanned settlement?

options.content: Residents have no legal title to the land
options.rationale: Correct: insecure tenure is a defining feature.

options.content: Every house has piped water and sewerage
options.rationale: Unplanned settlements lack such services.

options.content: Large plots with gardens and swimming pools
options.rationale: This describes low-density suburbs.

options.content: Wide tarred roads laid out by the council
options.rationale: Roads are usually narrow, unpaved paths.

explanation: Unplanned settlements lack permission, tenure and services.

stem: What is **in-situ upgrading**?

options.content: Improving a settlement where it stands
options.rationale: Correct: services are added without moving residents.

options.content: Moving residents to a new town
options.rationale: That is relocation.

options.content: Demolishing all informal homes
options.rationale: That is clearance.

options.content: Building high-rise offices on the site
options.rationale: That is redevelopment for commercial use.

explanation: Upgrading adds water, sanitation, roads and power in place.

stem: Why do many unplanned settlements develop on flood plains and wetlands?

options.content: The land has the best views in the city
options.rationale: Views are not the reason.

options.content: The council has built services there
options.rationale: Such areas are usually unserviced.

options.content: The land is unused because it is hazardous
options.rationale: Correct: nobody else wants it, so people can occupy it.

options.content: The land is the most expensive in town
options.rationale: Hazardous land is cheap or unclaimed.

explanation: Marginal, hazardous land is often the only land available to the poor.

stem: Which effect of unplanned settlements is **environmental**?

options.content: A busy informal economy
options.rationale: This is economic.

options.content: Polluted streams
options.rationale: Correct: this affects the natural environment.

options.content: Fear of eviction
options.rationale: This is social.

options.content: Strong community spirit
options.rationale: This is social.

explanation: Effects can be grouped as social, economic and environmental.

stem: Why does giving residents **security of tenure** often lead to better housing?

options.content: The council then builds every house for free
options.rationale: Tenure does not mean free houses.

options.content: It forces all residents to move away
options.rationale: Tenure lets residents stay.

options.content: It stops any new migrants from rural areas arriving in the city
options.rationale: It does not control migration.

options.content: Residents are willing to invest in homes they cannot lose
options.rationale: Correct: security encourages improvement.

explanation: People improve homes when they are sure they will stay.

stem: Which settlement on the south-eastern edge of Harare grew largely without planning and has been the focus of regularisation and upgrading?

options.content: Borrowdale
options.rationale: Borrowdale is a planned low-density suburb.

options.content: Mount Pleasant
options.rationale: Mount Pleasant is a planned low-density suburb.

options.content: Msasa
options.rationale: Msasa is an industrial area.

options.content: Epworth
options.rationale: Correct: it grew from a mission settlement into a large informal settlement.

explanation: Epworth is Harare's best-known example of regularisation and upgrading.

stem: A city has strict building standards requiring brick houses with tiled roofs on large plots. How might this contribute to unplanned settlements?

options.content: It makes every family able to afford a house of its own
options.rationale: Higher standards raise costs.

options.content: It stops people migrating to the city
options.rationale: Standards do not control migration.

options.content: It provides free land for all migrants
options.rationale: Standards do not provide land.

options.content: Legal houses become too expensive for poor families
options.rationale: Correct: high standards price the poor out of formal housing.

explanation: Unaffordable standards push the poor into informal housing.
hints: What do formal building standards do to the price of a house?

stem: Why is upgrading usually considered better than clearing an unplanned settlement?

options.content: It costs nothing at all
options.rationale: Upgrading needs funding.

options.content: It removes all residents from the city to new towns
options.rationale: Upgrading keeps residents.

options.content: It keeps communities and livelihoods in place
options.rationale: Correct: residents keep their homes, networks and businesses.

options.content: It needs no involvement from residents
options.rationale: Upgrading works best with community participation.

explanation: Clearance without alternatives moves the problem; upgrading improves conditions in place.
hints: What happens to people and livelihoods after each approach?

stem: In an unplanned settlement, homes are tightly packed, families cook on open fires and there are no roads. Which hazard is most increased?

options.content: Earth tremors
options.rationale: Earthquakes and tremors are not caused by housing density.

options.content: Fast-spreading fires
options.rationale: Correct: close-packed homes and no access for fire engines.

options.content: Prolonged drought
options.rationale: Drought is a climatic hazard.

options.content: Ground frost
options.rationale: Frost is a weather hazard unrelated to layout.

explanation: Density, open fires and poor access raise fire risk.
hints: Which hazard is most linked to close-packed homes with open fires and no roads?

stem: Many residents of unplanned settlements earn a living in the informal sector.
explanation: True. Vending, tailoring, carpentry and welding are common.

stem: Mbare is an unplanned settlement because it is a crowded high-density suburb.
explanation: False. Mbare is a planned high-density suburb with council services; crowding alone does not make an area unplanned.

stem: Match each improvement measure with what it does.

right.content: Provides new serviced plots for self-building
Small loans to improve homes or start businesses
Adds services where people already live

explanation: Each measure tackles a different problem.

stem: Complete the sentence.

payload.template: Informal settlements in Brazil are called {{blank:a}}. The legal right to stay on land without fear of eviction is called security of {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Favelas are Brazilian informal settlements; tenure is the right to occupy.

stem: A fictional informal settlement has 3,600 residents sharing 24 water standpipes (fictional data). How many people share each standpipe on average?
explanation: 3,600 ÷ 24 = 150 people per standpipe.

stem: Before upgrading, 210 of 1,400 households in a fictional settlement had a toilet. After upgrading, 980 had one (fictional data). By how many percentage points did the share of households with a toilet rise?
explanation: 15% → 70%: a rise of 55 percentage points.
hints: Find the increase in households with toilets.

stem: Explain **two** causes of unplanned settlements in towns of developing countries.

points.description: Rapid rural-urban migration / natural increase means population grows faster than housing.
Explains that the housing shortage leaves newcomers with nowhere legal to live.
Poverty: many cannot afford formal rents, house prices or building standards.
Explains that they therefore build cheaply on unused or hazardous land / weak planning control allows it.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Towns grow rapidly through migration and natural increase, faster than councils can build houses, so many newcomers have nowhere legal to live. Many are poor and cannot afford formal rents or the cost of building to council standards, so they build cheap shelters on unused land.

explanation: Two causes, each explained.

stem: Describe the social effects of living in an unplanned settlement.

points.description: Water-borne diseases (cholera, typhoid, diarrhoea) from unsafe water and poor sanitation.
Overcrowding spreads respiratory diseases such as TB.
Fire risk, crime and insecurity / fear of eviction.
Positive: strong community spirit, self-help groups and churches.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Unsafe water and pit latrines lead to cholera and diarrhoea, and crowded rooms spread TB. Fires spread quickly and residents live in fear of eviction and crime. However, many settlements have strong community groups that help each other.

explanation: Social effects concern people's health, safety and community.
hints: Think about water, sanitation, overcrowding and fire.

stem: With reference to a named example, evaluate the measures that can be used to improve unplanned settlements.

points.description: Names an example (e.g. Epworth, Harare) and describes its conditions.
Clearance/demolition: removes unsafe structures but destroys homes and livelihoods; problem moves elsewhere (e.g. 2005 operation).
In-situ upgrading: water, sanitation, roads in place; keeps communities; needs funding.
Regularisation and tenure: encourages residents to invest; requires surveying and fair processes.
Site-and-service / low-cost housing: legal homes; may be unaffordable or far from jobs.
Community participation and savings groups improve success.
Supported judgement on the most effective combination.

levels.descriptor: Developed, accurate explanation of several relevant points, supported by a located example or the resource, with a clear judgement or conclusion where the question asks for one.
Some explanation of relevant points, partly developed; an example or resource evidence is used in general terms; any judgement is simple or one-sided.
Simple statements or a list of points with little explanation; no example or only a name.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Epworth on the edge of Harare grew largely without planning, with many homes lacking piped water and sewerage. Clearance, as in Zimbabwe's 2005 operation, removes structures but destroys homes and livelihoods; a UN report estimated around 700,000 people were affected, and many simply moved elsewhere. In-situ upgrading, adding water points, drains and roads, improves health while keeping communities and businesses in place, but it needs sustained funding. Regularisation, surveying plots and giving residents tenure, encourages families to build better homes, and in Epworth community savings groups helped map the settlement and contribute. Site-and-service schemes give legal plots but may be too expensive for the poorest or too far from jobs. The most effective approach combines regularisation and upgrading with community participation, and relocation only from genuinely hazardous sites.

explanation: Evaluate several measures and judge.
hints: Compare clearance, relocation, upgrading and regularisation.

stem:
Table 1 compares a fictional unplanned settlement (U) with a fictional planned high-density suburb (H) in the same city (fictional data).

| Indicator | U | H |
|---|---|---|
| Homes with piped water (%) | 8 | 72 |
| Homes using a pit latrine or open space (%) | 85 | 10 |
| Homes with legal title or lease (%) | 5 | 90 |
| Cases of diarrhoea per 1,000 children last year | 260 | 95 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: How many more cases of diarrhoea per 1,000 children were there in U than in H?

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which indicator best explains the higher rate of diarrhoea in U?

options.content: Homes with legal title or lease
options.rationale: Tenure affects investment, not disease directly.

options.content: Homes using a pit latrine or open space
options.rationale: Correct: poor sanitation spreads water-borne disease.

options.content: The number of children in each settlement
options.rationale: The rate is already per 1,000 children.

options.content: The distance of each settlement from the CBD
options.rationale: The table does not give distance.

parts.explanation: Sanitation (with water supply) is the direct cause.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Using Table 1, describe the differences in living conditions between U and H.

points.description: Piped water: 8% in U compared with 72% in H.
Sanitation: 85% use pit latrines or open space in U against 10% in H.
Tenure: 5% have title in U against 90% in H.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Only 8% of homes in U have piped water against 72% in H. In U 85% use pit latrines or open spaces, compared with 10% in H, and only 5% have legal title compared with 90% in H.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Suggest **three** measures that would improve conditions in U.

points.description: Install communal or household water points / piped water.
Build toilets and sewers or ventilated pit latrines; drains.
Regularise plots and give residents tenure / health education / microcredit.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The council could install standpipes and later piped water, build toilet blocks and drains, and survey the plots to give residents leases so they invest in their homes.

parts.explanation: Measures should match the problems in the data.

explanation: This item practises comparing settlements with data.
hints: Compare U with H for each indicator.

stem: Description of a fictional city: an unplanned settlement of about 9,000 people lies on the flood plain of a river 2 km from the main industrial area. Homes are made of timber and metal sheets; residents collect water from the river and from two boreholes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** reasons why the settlement grew at this site.

points.description: Close to the industrial area, so residents can walk to work.
The flood plain was unused / unclaimed land, with water from the river.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It is only 2 km from the factories, so people can walk to work, and the flood plain was empty land that no one else wanted, with water nearby.

parts.explanation: Link site to jobs and land availability.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: On average, how many people share each borehole?

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe **three** risks to residents of living on this site.

points.description: Flooding destroys homes and belongings.
River water is polluted, causing water-borne disease.
Fire spreads through timber homes / eviction because the land is not theirs.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The river can flood and wash away homes. River water may be polluted, causing cholera and diarrhoea. Timber homes burn easily, and residents could be evicted.

explanation: This item practises reasoning about the site and risks of unplanned settlements.
hints: Think about why people chose this site and what risks it brings.
